text:
Ideas on How to Refresh Your Home Office with Stone Veneer

You spend large swaths of time in your home office; it should be a welcoming environment that helps you be productive and effective. It should also provide an air of professionalism that keeps you focused and motivated.

What if there was a simple, easy design enhancement you could make that would achieve all the above? The great news is that adding some stone veneer flair to your home office can go a long way in refreshing and modernizing an otherwise ‘blah’ home workspace.

To help jumpstart your creative juices, GenStone is serving up a few fun, innovative ideas for using faux stone to ‘level up’ your home office.

Idea #1: Build Out a Home Office Accent Wall

Accent walls do a terrific job of breaking up the monotony of a home office. Regardless what your interior design style is, there’s a GenStone faux stone veneer solution that will go great with your existing decor, color scheme, and home office layout.

Here’s how to get started with your stone veneer accent wall project:

- Pick a wall. This is often the most difficult choice to make. Which wall will become your accent wall? When making this decision, consider where your eyes are drawn when you first enter your home office space. Try to choose a wall that is opposed or counter to wherever the room’s focal point is. This will help to ‘even out’ the overall texture of the home office.

- Take measurements. When working with GenStone faux stone products, we recommend using the Linear Feet measurement method when determining how many stone veneer panels, ledgers, and trim you’ll need for your new accent wall. For more information on how to determine the volume of GenStone material you’ll need, please visit our “How Much Do I Need” page .

- Decide whether brick veneer or stacked stone would look best. Our brick veneer panels come in four colors and provide a rugged, industrial look. Alternatively, GenStone stacked stone products offer a more randomized yet structured look that goes great with many existing home office aesthetics.

- Order your faux stone and follow the installation instructions. At GenStone, we make it easy to bring an authentic stone or brick look to any home office. Our ‘How to Install’ page offers clear, step-by-step video guides to aid you during the installation process. And, our support team is always willing to help with any obstacles you might encounter along the way.

The best part about adding an accent wall to your home office is that the entire project can be completed in a single weekend. Easy!

Kenai Faux Stone Accent Wall

Idea #2: Home Office Wainscotting with Faux Stone

This idea is a little more complicated than adding an accent wall, and that’s because special attention needs to be paid to cornering, trimming, and mating of shiplap edges.

However, the steps are similar:

- Measure the linear feet of the area to be wainscotted. Generally speaking, it’s a good idea to wainscot the entire room, as opposed to performing the treatment on just a single wall or two.

- Determine the height of the wainscotted faux stone . For home offices, a 3 foot-high wainscot makes for a pleasing, design-friendly addition. Be sure to factor in the additional height provided by the ledgers (3.5 inches).

- Order the GenStone products you need and follow the installation instructions. As mentioned above, our support resources can make the entire process fast and intuitive, even for first-time faux stone installers.

Even though wainscotting requires less faux stone paneling due to the smaller square footage of treated wallspace, the additional cornering and ledger installations demand a little extra attention. The result will be worth the extra effort, however, and we think you’ll love the transformation of your home office space.

Stratford Stacked Stone Exterior Wainscoting

Idea #3: Liven Up Counter Space with a Stacked Stone Backsplash

Does your home office have a counter like this one? Consider adding a faux stone backsplash using one of the six available color choices.

Backsplashes require the least amount of faux stone paneling, and the overall project can realistically be completed in just a few hours.

If your workspace is integrated into a counter, why not add the backsplash to the area behind your computer monitor? Doing this can provide a higher contrast working area, which could go a long way in helping you maintain your productivity.

When you’re more comfortable in your home office, you’re more likely to enjoy the time you spend there. To get started on your faux stone project, contact GenStone today.

title: Infographic on Improving Home Energy Efficiency | GenStone
description: Improving your home energy efficiency doesn't need to be a daunting endeavor. Try these 5 simple and cost-effective home projects for a greener home.
text:
Infographic: Home Projects to Increase Energy Efficiency
Energy Efficient House Ideas

Time and Cost Effective Home Projects

In the past, the term “home energy efficiency” brought visions of expensive solar panels, giant wind turbines or quirky lifestyle changes. But as the strategy has reached the mainstream, the public has come to better understand what energy efficiency is and how it benefits everyone. In addition to cutting down on pollution and conserving natural resources, increasing home energy efficiency is a valuable investment that saves consumers money. If you’re just starting to look at how to make your home more energy efficient, know that there are several time and cost effective home projects that can immediately decrease consumption as well as the price of your energy and utilities bills.

Home Energy Infographic

Do It Yourself Energy Efficiency Ideas

You don’t have to be a contractor to buy and install green building materials. In fact, there are hundreds of home improvement ideas that will make your house more energy efficient. Most energy saving projects can be completed in a few spare hours, including improving these three areas with five easy tasks

Install Low-flow Water Fixtures

Don’t put so much pressure on yourself.

Switching out showerheads and faucets is a simple task that can make a big difference in your water consumption. Low-flow water fixtures are designed to produce a strong flow of water while using less water than a standard water fixture. Low-flow fixtures run anywhere from $15-$30 and can be installed without the help of a professional.

Save Electricity Save Money

Swap out those old light bulbs and appliances.

Replacing Light Bulbs

Electric lighting represents a sizable chunk of a home energy bill. Update your light fixtures and bulbs with halogen incandescent, CFL or LED light bulbs. According to the US Department of Energy, switching to these more efficient bulbs can save you $75 a year. Take your time choosing what bulbs to buy as newer light bulbs and fixtures give you a variety of choices when it comes to color and intensity.

Replace Old Appliances

Refrigerators, washers and dishwashers use a lot of energy and water, especially if they’re more than ten years old. Federal law has forced many manufacturers to produce more efficient home appliances, which means updating your appliances could make a big difference. If replacing all of your major appliances at the same time is too expensive, consider replacing the refrigerator first, as older refrigerators are big energy hogs.

Green Building Materials

Add the look of stone and increase R-Value.

Many homes were built before energy efficiency was a focus, meaning green building materials weren’t used during construction. Update your home’s look and efficiency with the installation of faux stone panels . Adding faux stone can increase the R-value of your siding, which is a measure of insulation. These easy-to-install panels are an attractive upgrade to your home’s exterior that could even increase the value of your home.

title: Our Favorite Faux Brick Design Ideas | Faux Brick Fireplaces | GenStone
description: A faux brick fireplace is just one of many great stacked stone designs. Learn more about our favorite faux brick design ideas in this blog from GenStone.
text:
Our Favorite Faux Brick Design Ideas

Faux brick is a great way to add layers of character and depth to your home’s design, whether it’s inside or outside the house.

With a fantastic variety of styles, ranging from classic red brick to deep, stone-colored veneers, there’s so much opportunity to be creative when it comes to installing faux brick panels.

Give your kitchen or bedroom a quick makeover, or create a rustic fireplace in the living room. To inspire your next DIY project , here are our favorite faux brick design ideas that you can put into action today.

Give Your Living Room a Faux Brick Makeover

It’s a simple design idea, but it’s the simplicity of adding a faux brick wall to your living room that makes it such a popular interior makeover move.

If you’re looking to add a unique touch to your living space or to breathe a breath of fresh air into your home, then you can have a faux brick wall up in as little as a few hours.

You can cover all your existing living room walls in faux brick, for uniformity, or you can create a much more interesting style of your own by only paneling one wall, and leaving the others as they are.

Faux Stone Brick Accent Wall in a Bed & Breakfast Waiting Room

Create a Focal Point in the Room

If you’re not ready to faux brick an entire wall, then why not take a minimalist approach and use faux brick to create a focal point in the room?

Faux brick, especially in deep shades of red, can create a vivid point of focus in a living area, or even in the bedroom. Just add faux brick to a small area of the wall, and it immediately draws the attention of anyone entering the room.

You can use the focal point just to stand out, or you can use it as a space to hang a television or a work of art; it’s totally up to you.

Faux Brick Fireplaces

If it’s a faux brick focal point you’re looking to craft, then look no further than building a faux brick fireplace.

If you already have a fireplace built into the wall, you can simply add faux brick panels in a style of your choice around the existing structure. It’s a quick and easy job that instantly changes the character of the room.

If you are looking to build a new fireplace, then you can incorporate faux brick into the overall design.

Faux Brick Pillars

Faux brick pillars and columns can be a fantastic way to add character to the corners of your room or to hide structural supports inside the house. They look great, and they provide a cover for an otherwise bland part of the home.

You can also incorporate faux brick pillars and columns outside the house, too. They can add a new dimension to a doorway, or you can even use them at the entrance to the property. Pillars and columns are also perfect for designing new, faux brick mailboxes.

Hidden Doors

A classic use for faux brick panels is to craft a concealed or hidden doorway inside or outside of the home.

If you need a secure area or just want to hide away every now and then, then concealed entrances can be covered up using faux brick walls.

Faux Brick Wall Art

When it comes to faux brick design ideas, you’re only really limited by your imagination. There are countless projects you can work on, and you can even get creative and artsy.

Faux brick can be used to work unique art designs into the walls themselves. You can merge different styles of brick, or work with multiple materials to create different designs. You can create lettering or even entire scenes using a combination of plain walls and faux brick.

There are so many great options, and that’s why faux brick is one of our favorite materials to work with when it comes to design work!

Classic Faux Brick Corner Piece

Why Choose GenStone?

Our favorite faux brick design ideas can all be recreated in your own home. GenStone’s faux brick panels are wonderfully easy to install, all you need are a few simple tools and a few inspired ideas.

Our unique panel systems make faux brick a great DIY project, while our designs are all molded using real brick, giving them an authentic, appealing look, inside or outside the house.

Get in touch with our friendly, professional staff, if you’re looking for more creative ideas or if you’re ready to put one of our favorite faux brick designs into action!

Shed Skirting Ideas You Can Complete in a Weekend

- Faux stone is less expensive. Brick or natural stone materials are very costly, especially when the labor expenses are taken into consideration. With faux stone or faux brick paneling from GenStone, you can easily cut your costs in half (or more), and you’ll have an equally attractive, aesthetically pleasing outcome.

- Installation is easy for DIY-ers. To install a faux stone shed skirt, you don’t have to be a Master Brickmason. Some simple hand tools and a little expert instruction from the GenStone support staff are all you need to complete this project in a single weekend.

- GenStone faux stone and faux brick shed skirts are waterproof. Did you know that by adding a faux stone shed skirt , you’ll actually be improving your shed’s protection against the elements? It’s true!

For a more attractive-looking shed that fits well with other design elements of your home, a faux stone shed skirt is a fantastic idea.

Here are a few shed skirting ideas to get you started.

The One-Foot “Short Skirt”

As you may already know, GenStone faux stone panels measure 12” in height and 42” in length. This sizing makes it easy to determine how many panels you’ll need to skirt your entire shed.

Kenai Stacked Stone Panels

To install a one-foot ‘short skirt’ on your shed, you’ll want to follow these simple steps:

- Measure the length of each side of your shed, in inches, and then divide by 42. This will give you the total number of faux stone panels you’re going to need to install a one-foot shed skirt. If you wind up with a fraction or decimal, always round up to the nearest panel.

- Don’t forget the trim and ledgers! Trim and ledgers can be used either horizontally or vertically, and they’re engineered to be used with the integrated shiplap edges built into GenStone faux stone panels.

- Obtain the GenStone materials you need for your shed skirt, and then lay them down in front of the surfaces that are going to be treated. This will help you to visualize where to make your cuts and what panel transitions make the most sense for your shed’s look and feel.

- Plan for obstacles. If your shed has hose spigots, electrical boxes, or other physical surface interruptions, these are going to need to be accounted for in the cutting of your GenStone faux stone panels.

- Install the panels! Start your panel run from the most convenient corner. You’ll want to be sure to completely secure each panel to the wall with shiplap and face screws as you move along. Remember that the stone undersides are often the best locations for face screws.

After you’ve installed the exterior shed skirt, how about moving to the interior?

Interior Shed Skirt

The inside of a backyard shed or storage building doesn’t have to be boring and fashionably neglected. If you’ve gone to the effort of adding an exterior faux stone skirt to your shed, why not go for enhancing the interior, as well?

There is only one significant difference between the use of interior and exterior faux stone panels for shed skirting, and that is how the corners are treated.

For an exterior shed skirt, you’ll only need outside corner pieces of faux stone.

For an interior shed skirt, you’ll only need inside corner pieces of faux stone.

Both inside and outside faux stone panels contain the same shiplap edge accommodations that are needed to make the entire system work well together.

After you’ve added both and interior and exterior shed skirt, you’ll be able to enjoy a fresh, bold new look to your shed, whether you’re on the inside of it or on the outside!

Because of how easy it is to work with GenStone faux stone products , both an interior and and exterior shed treatment can easily be completed in a single weekend.

When you’re ready to breathe new life into your shed, it’s time to dust off those hand tools and get to work!

text:
Shed Skirting Made Easy with Faux Stone

There are lots of great design ideas that can transform your backyard shed into a more attractive, bolder-looking structure. You could upgrade the siding, enhance the roof, add some barn doors, or throw on a fresh coat of paint.

Of all the things you could do to upgrade the look of your shed, giving it a faux stone skirting treatment ranks among the most effective and easiest. In this article, we’re giving you some great shed skirting ideas you can use to give your shed the makeover it needs. And, by following the installation guidelines on our ‘How to Install’ page, you can complete a shed skirting project in a single afternoon. It’s a lot easier than you may think!

What Is ‘Shed Skirting', Anyway?

If you’re new to the concept of skirting, here’s a quick description:

Most utility and storage sheds are built on concrete foundations or flat, wood bases. Depending on the size and volume of the shed, it could be supported with as much as two feet of material rise. Some sheds are built on stilts that help protect the shed subfloor from pests, corrosion, and water damage.

‘Skirting’ is a term used to describe the installation of facade material that covers the shed foundation or base. Shed skirting is a lot like wainscoting, however much less material is used as only the base of the shed is treated. Most shed skirts are smaller than two feet in height.

Stratford Stacked Stone Shed Wainscoting

There are plenty of great shed skirting ideas out there, from using lattice work fencing to barn wood or installing vinyl siding to cover the exposed concrete or wood foundation. While these can be fantastic design additions for some sheds, using faux stone from GenStone is affordable, easy, and longer-lasting than traditional shed skirting treatments. The reason for this lies in the construction of GenStone faux stone panels: every piece is constructed using strong, lightweight polyurethane foam that looks just like real stacked stone!

So, by applying a shed skirt with GenStone faux stone, you get the look and feel of real stone without the cost, labor, and time investment that real stone would require. It’s a win-win!

How to Complete a Faux Stone Shed Skirting Project

To plan out your shed skirting project, you’ll first want to determine which stacked stone style will work best with the design aesthetic of your shed.

You have two courses of action, here:

- Choose among our selection of stacked stone color themes . If you’d like to see what your shed skirt will look like with a certain color choice, just send us a picture of your shed along with the color you’d like (i.e., Stratford or Kenai), and we’ll create a digital mockup for you.

- Get custom-colored stacked faux stone panels directly from GenStone. To do this, just send us an image of the color you want, and we’ll assist you in the process of having a truly unique color-themed panel set built just for you, including corner panels, return panels, trim, and ledgers if necessary.

Once you’ve determined what color style you’d like to go with, it’s time to take some measurements. All you need to do here is take a linear foot measurement of the base of your shed, and add 5% to the total before placing your order.

For tips on how to take measurements in preparation for a faux stone shed skirting project, visit our ‘How to Measure’ guide .

Once you’ve obtained the GenStone material you want to use for your shed skirt, it’s time for installation. Depending on the surface you’ll be treating, you’ll want to use either an industrial-grade adhesive or non-corrosive deck screws to affix your faux stone panels. For concrete foundations, the adhesive method works best. For wood foundations, either adhesive or deck screws will suffice.

Keep in mind that GenStone faux stone full panels measure 11” in height with a 1” shiplap edge. This is typically tall enough to cover most shed foundations, although yours might be taller. Because our faux stone panels are made out of polyurethane material, they’re easy to cut using a basic handsaw, radial saw, or table saw. So, you never have to worry about oversizing your project, as every piece can be cut-to-size in mere seconds.

title: Stacked Stone Water Fountain Ideas | Faux Stone Fountains | GenStone
description: This latest blog post from GenStone features stacked stone water fountain ideas. Learn how to spruce up your yard with a faux stone fountain and more!
text:
Stacked Stone Water Fountain Ideas for Your Outdoor Landscape

Whoever said every outdoor water foundation has to be the same?

GenStone faux stone panels, corner pieces, and trim can be combined in creative ways to enhance the look and feel of virtually any water fountain. No matter what kind of aesthetic you’re going for in the creation of your outdoor water fountain, GenStone has the natural-looking stone veneer solution to suit you.

In this article, we’re going to present a few unique water fountain design ideas to help you get the creative juices flowing. These are just a few concepts we’ve come up with—remember that the greatest part about faux stone is that you can modify the materials you use as well as their configuration to result in a final water fountain that expresses your individual style.

Take these ideas and turn them into your own creation!

Before You Get Started

Every outdoor water fountain has at least three component parts:

- The water pump. There are many submersible water pumps to choose from. We like this one from PonicsPumps . For slower-flowing fountains, choose a Gallons-per-Hour rating (GPH) of 100 or lower. Larger fountains with more water volume can go up to 400 GPH or even higher.

- Water tubing. Vinyl or PVC tubing can be used in conjunction with most of the more common water pumps on the market. It’s important to run the tubing so that a ‘closed circuit’ of water flow is achieved.

- Power supply. Remember that your outdoor water fountain will need 120V AC power to operate, in most cases. Take a moment to strategize about how you’re going to provide this power to the fountain.

Now that you’ve got the essentials ( including enough GenStone faux stone paneling!), it’s time to begin!

Stratford Stacked Stone Water Feature

Idea #1: Faux Stone-Flanked Multi-Tier Water Feature

Because the water within your outdoor fountain can be pumped as far as 100 feet or more from the pump itself, this opens up lots of design opportunities.

For a multi-tiered water feature, use GenStone faux stone panels and corner pieces to create the ‘shell’ of the fountain. This is best done using treated plywood or timber for the basic structure, and then adding the stacked stone GenStone panels using your choice of wood screws.

Within the ‘shell’, you’ll want to create at least two different stages for water accumulation. Get creative here! Consider using a natural stone bowl or basin with a runoff that feeds another basin of a larger or smaller size.

Keep in mind where the lowest point of your outdoor water fountain will be, and be sure to place your pump in this location.

Idea #2: Single-Pedestal Stacked Stone Fountain

Want a simpler yet equally elegant outdoor water fountain? How about building your own single-pedestal stacked stone pool fountain using GenStone pillar kits?

The sky’s the limit with this idea. Simply follow these steps:

- Build a hollow, 8” square post using PVC, vinyl siding, or any other waterproof material. This will serve as the pedestal for the fountain, and it will be secured in the center of the holding pool.

- Add GenStone stacked stone pillar veneers. Installation is a snap! Our pillar kits are made to work perfectly with 8” square posts, and the panels themselves naturally interweave, giving the appearance of real, stacked stone!

- Run your fountain pump tubing through the flat or peaked pillar cap (your choice). Then, simply let the waterfall down all four corners of the pedestal, accumulate in the holding pool, and recirculate using your water pump.

These single-pedestal outdoor water faux stone fountains can double as birdbaths with the addition of a washbasin added to the top. Use your imagination to create an attractive, natural-looking water feature that complements the rest of your outdoor living space.

Need Support? We’ve Got Your Back!

At GenStone, we’re committed to equipping you with the materials and know-how you need to complete the outdoor water fountain project of your dreams.

If you find yourself in need of support during the installation of any GenStone stacked stone product, feel free to reach out to our team for prompt assistance. We’ll share with you the best practices for installing GenStone faux stone panels, corner pieces, and trim so your outdoor water fountain looks great!

Just head over to our Contact Page , give us a brief description of your project, and we’ll do all we can to provide outstanding support to help you reach your goals. We look forward to hearing from you and seeing what kind of outdoor water fountain ideas you’re able to bring to life!

title: The 4 Best Backyard Faux Stone Gazebo Ideas | GenStone

text:
The 4 Best Backyard Faux Stone Gazebo Ideas

Ready to do something with your backyard gazebo?

What can you do except add another coat of paint?

Whatever you use your gazebo for, it’s very easy to add some contrast and texture with faux stone panels. It’s hard to deny the appeal of stacked stone, the imperfectly perfect edges, combined with irregular joint lines.

It creates a very relaxed and casual feel. Faux stone is a superior choice over natural stone, since faux stone panels install easily with basic tools and skills, and you can complete any of these very budget-friendly DIY projects over the course of a single weekend.

While most gazebos are just a group of columns supporting a roof, there are several ways to use faux stone to give your gazebo some architectural interest and boost its visual appeal at the same time. Whether your backyard gazebo is made of wood or metal, faux stone panels will work harmoniously with both options.

With six different styles of stacked stone to choose from, GenStone’s faux stone panels will complement your gazebo’s existing style and design.

#1: Transform Those Boring Walls

One of the simplest and most dramatic uses of faux stone is to transform those “ho-hum” half-walls between your gazebo posts.

This will provide some privacy if you use your gazebo for a hot tub area. Don’t worry, GenStone faux stone panels are 99.9% waterproof, so they are perfect for the hot tub area. If your gazebo uses lattice panels between the posts, simply cover the lattice with plywood, and then install your stylish stacked stone panels directly to the plywood.

Here are a couple of ideas to use stacked faux stone panels on your gazebo walls.

- One option is to cover all of the half-walls, except at the doorway(s). This would be a full wraparound of your gazebo with faux stone panels. If you think that might be too much stacked stone for the size of your gazebo, consider covering every other wall with the faux stacked stone.

- You could also use faux stone to cover the wood base of your gazebo (if applicable) to create a stacked stone “skirt” that wraps around your entire gazebo base. This will create the illusion of a stone foundation, adding some subtle interest and depth to the structure.

#2: The Stacked Stone Pillar

Another great idea is to wrap just the gazebo posts with GenStone’s pillar kits.

They come with premade corners, so there’s no difficult cutting or math calculations involved. These faux stone kits are made to fit an 8” square column, and they install in mere minutes.

After that, add a flat or peaked pillar cap to complete the transformation of your backyard faux stone gazebo .

Depending on the size and number of posts your gazebo has, consider these ideas:

- Use only 2 pillar kits to establish the gazebo entry.

- Use 4 pillar kits to create a defined entry and exit.

- Use GenStone faux stone pillar kits on every post of your gazebo.

- Create 4 “legs”, add plywood and a countertop to create a table for dining, or a food prep area for your barbecue or outdoor kitchen gazebo.

#3: A Stacked Stone Water Feature

Stone water features are a great addition to almost any area, and your backyard gazebo is no exception. The sound of slowly moving water has a calming and relaxing effect on almost everyone. Design your water feature using walls to hide the electrical connection and the pump motor, and simply cover the exterior plywood surface with faux stone panels.

You could go with a simple square box fountain that bubbles out of the top, or maybe have a chute coming through the wall where the water cascades off the edge. The possibilities are endless!

Stratford Stacked Stone outdoor water feature

#4: An Outdoor Fireplace

If your gazebo is large enough, you might consider adding a faux stone outdoor fireplace.

Having heat readily available will allow you to use your gazebo well into the fall season, not just during spring and summer months. GenStone’s faux stone panels can work with all fireplace types, and they are available in a Class A Fire-rated version, as well.

To create a true natural stone fireplace would be very expensive, messy (lots of mortar and stones), and time-consuming.

With the faux stone option, simply cover the fireplace substrate with our natural looking stone panels to get the same stunning results.

Whether you choose a traditional height fireplace, a double-sided fireplace, or the floor-to-ceiling option, you will be amazed at the visual impact created with faux stone panels.

title: Using Faux Stone on Angled or Irregular Walls | GenStone
description: This blog post from GenStone looks at how faux stone ideas for angled walls. Click here to learn the ins and outs of faux stone curved walls!
text:
Using Faux Stone on Angled or Irregular Walls

Faux stone is the perfect choice for angled or irregular walls, inside or outside the home. A versatile, light, yet astoundingly realistic-looking material, faux stone panels are easy to work with and can be installed with only a little DIY experience.

At GenStone, our faux stone panels can easily be cut and shaped to cover almost any style (and angle) of wall in your home. They are popular additions to archways, angled ceilings, or even curved walls, adding a dramatic element to the aesthetic of your property while being quite simple to build.

To inspire your design ideas, our design experts at GenStone are sharing some tips on using faux stone on angled or irregular walls.

Can I Use Faux Stone on Angled and Irregular Walls?

If you’re reading our latest article, then you’re likely wondering: is it even possible to use faux stone on angled and irregular walls? The simple answer is yes!

Angled or irregular walls can prove to be a common problem for DIY enthusiasts looking to modify their interior (or exterior) home design. Angled and irregular walls are surprisingly common, too.

Many properties have angled ceilings and walls in rooms on upper floors, the most obvious examples being found in attic conversions. You might also have arched doorways or irregular wall designs that incorporate curves or angles to give them a unique, artistic look.

Faux stone can be cut to measure, ensuring that panels don’t just need to be fixed on vertical, or even flat wall surfaces.

Is It Difficult to Affix Faux Stone Panels to Irregular Walls?

The great thing about using faux stone on your irregular or angled walls is that faux stone panels are simple to install. Once they are up, they are long-lasting, robust, and in need of little maintenance.

Once you’ve chosen your faux stone style (keep reading for a few ideas) then you’ll need to take your measurements to know how much material you need to order.

To cut the faux stone panels to size, you’ll just need a saw. To fix the boards in place, all you require for GenStone panels are the right screws and a power drill. Detailed instructions are provided of course, but the unique paneling system means that once cut, everything slots quickly into place.

The lightweight nature of the faux stone makes it great for angled walls that wouldn’t otherwise be able to support the weight of real stone or brick veneers. For this type of angled wall, you can work from the bottom upwards, ensuring that every panel is securely fastened.

You can even tackle curved walls, although you will need to have a little more patience and DIY experience than for a simpler angled wall. For curved walls, you need to install the faux stone panels in smaller segments, as you need to work your designs into the curve.

This takes time and more precise cutting to make sure that the faux stone follows the natural contours of the curve and doesn’t produce sharper angles or disjointed seams.

Faux Stone Design Ideas for Your Irregular Walls

Faux stone panels require just a little experience and only a few tools to properly install, yet one of the best things about them is the dramatic effect they can produce in your home.

Our experts here at GenStone have plenty of design ideas when it comes to using faux stone. For starters, you can complement a fantastic range of existing interior designs using the natural stone patterns we have in our repertoire.

Or you can shake things up by installing a style of faux stone that’s in sharp contrast to the rest of the room.

You can create a talking point by using faux stone on your angled ceiling, or you can make a unique focal point in the kitchen by creating a breakfast bar set against a masterfully designed, curved wall.

Iron Ore Stacked Stone Kitchen Island

Some of our most popular faux stone styles to use in your designs include the classic Keystone Stacked Stone look if you desire an unobtrusive look, or the Iron Ore Stacked Stone if you prefer a sharp, dark, and contrasting color scheme.

Why Choose GenStone?

GenStone offers a fantastic range of faux stone designs that make for an unbeatable addition to your next interior or exterior design projects . Our unique faux stone paneling systems are not only easy to install, but they are all cast from natural stone, for an authentic appeal you just can’t find elsewhere.

Our highly professional team of faux stone experts are ready to help you today. Contact our friendly staff to find out how we can help you!

title: Faux Stone Designs | Stacked Stone Designs | GenStone
description: This blog post from GenStone explores the inspiration behind our faux stone and stacked stone designs. Click here to learn more!
text:
Where in the World Did Our Stacked Stone Designs Come From?

If you’ve never used GenStone faux stone panels before, you probably have a lot of questions. Some of the most common questions we receive are:

“How many panels do I need for my project?”

“Is it difficult to install GenStone?”

“Are these faux stone panels waterproof?”

“Can they be used outside?”

Etc., etc..

While these are all great questions, a recent one we received from one of our customers was this:

“Where did you get the inspiration for your stacked stone panel designs?”

What a great question!

There is actually a fair amount of history behind each of the faux stone panel designs currently available from GenStone. Each of them has their own unique backstory, and three of them in particular have their roots in geographical locations.

In this article, we’re going on an exotic journey around the world to explain the genesis of three of our most popular stacked faux stone panels: Kenai , Stratford , and Keystone .

Kenai

One of our distributors in Alaska is Spenard Builders Supply , a retailer of building materials and home improvement hardware. Spenard does a fantastic job supplying DIY-ers and contractors with the essentials they need to complete their projects in locations throughout Alaska.

One of Spenard’s flagship locations is in Kenai, Alaska, a coastal city just a few miles southwest of Anchorage. When we visited this location for the first time, we were awestruck by the natural beauty that surrounds this part of the state. The hilltops and mountains in Kenai are bedecked by some of the most beautiful, earthen colors we’ve ever seen: deep browns, subdued charcoals, and raw whites. After our very first trip there, we knew we had to replicate these colors and bring them to our customers.

That’s when we got our designers together in a room, sat down with our color palettes, and went to work creating the Kenai stacked stone color theme . The response from our customers has been fantastic, and Kenai continues to be one of our best-selling faux stone color choices.

Kenai Stacked Stone

Stratford

When the GenStone design team went about creating our iconic Stratford faux stone panels , they wanted to convey a sense of elegance, permanence, and timelessness.

So, they took to pouring over world maps in search of a locale that brings all of these elements together in a single color theme. Their search ended when they discovered a small suburb of Birmingham, England known as Stratford-upon-Avon.

This is the birthplace of Shakespeare, and it’s replete with centuries-old buildings that have stood the test of time. Everywhere you look, you see design inspirations from Old England, and the colors are authentic, strong, and noble.

The GenStone Stratford faux stone panel is an excellent choice for those who want an understated yet charming blend of earth tones including slate, rose, and beige hues.

Keystone

So far, we’ve journeyed to Alaska and the UK to find just the right colors to incorporate into our hallmark faux stone panels. Now, it’s time to jetset to the Rocky Mountains of Colorado.

GenStone is headquartered in Littleton, Colorado, a southwestern suburb of Denver. This is where we got our start, and it’s safe to say we owe a lot to the inspirational beauty of the area. Traveling from our headquarters west into the mountains, it’s about a two-hour drive to reach one of Colorado’s most sought-after vacation destinations: Keystone.

For roughly half of the year, vacationers head to Keystone for world-class skiing and a multitude of other snowsports. However, after the snow melts, the Keystone area reveals a multi-chromatic splendor that you just can’t find anywhere else.

Keystone’s spring- and summer-time geography is peppered with burgundies, beiges, and slate colors, a combination that lends itself well to the immersive, natural atmosphere here. Catching those colors and making them a part of our Keystone faux stone panels is something we’re incredibly proud of.

Keystone Stacked Stone

More Color Options, More Value...All from GenStone!

It’s difficult to say what our customers love most about our faux stone panels. The ease of installation, the lightweight, durable material, the attractive color themes—it all adds up to exceptional value from the leader in faux stone: GenStone!

Don’t forget that we’re now offering custom-colored faux stone panels that are hand-painted by our design staff. So, if none of our pre-formulated color themes strike your fancy, get in touch with us and let us know what color you’d like for your faux stone project. We’ll work with you to ensure that the faux panels you need are a perfect fit for your project.

text:
Why Faux Stone is Great for Trade Show Displays

When putting yourself and your company on display at a trade show, it’s important to give off a memorable, professional first impression.

There are many ways to do this. Flashy marketing graphics, giveaways, and eye-catching banners or posters are all common methods of making a splash at a trade show. But, have you considered the ‘wow factor’ that can come with using faux stone as part of your trade show display?

If not, allow us to explain why using our high-quality, durable faux stone panels can enhance your presence at your next trade show or other networking event.

Not only can our faux stone materials embolden your trade show displays, they’re also easy to work with and no specialized labor is required to have them installed. This makes using faux stone for trade show displays something any company can invest in as part of a creative approach to in-person marketing.

Say ‘Bye' to Boring Displays

If you’ve spent any amount of time at a recent trade show, you’ve probably seen a lot of the same few booth setups. Even though there are dozens of trade show display manufacturers out there, they all seem to provide the same, cookie-cutter display arrangement: a backlit vinyl marketing backdrop with maybe a small, center island for displaying brochures and product information. That’s it.

Trade show displays don’t have to be this boring!

Here’s why adding GenStone faux stone material to your trade show display can set you apart from the rest of the trade show booths:

- The look of real stone signifies strength and permanence. GenStone faux stone is made from molds of real stone, and every panel is hand-painted to look like genuine stacked stone. This gives the panels a strong, rugged appearance that inspires confidence.

- GenStone faux stone panels are incredibly lightweight and durable. If you were to use real stone to accentuate your trade show display, you’d wind up with a final product that would weigh potentially hundreds of pounds. Alternatively, GenStone faux stone composed of ultra-lightweight polyurethane foam, a substance that is as tough as it is light.Because GenStone panels are so light, the costs you incur from shipping your trade show display won’t be affected much, if at all.

- Faux stone gives display viewers a feeling of being in a safe, solid structure. We hear this a lot from our customers: GenStone faux stone makes them feel secure! This can have a positive effect at trade shows, where it’s important to put booth visitors at ease so business conversations can flow naturally.

Keystone Stacked Stone in a business setting

If you think it’ll take days or weeks to install GenStone faux stone panels on your trade show display, think again! For a standard, 10′ x 10′ trade show display, GenStone faux stone panels could be installed in just a few hours. And, with the installation resources you’ll find on our website, you’ll have all the resources you’ll need to complete a professional installation job.

New! Faux Stone to Match Your Brand

If you have a unique color palette that is part of your marketing materials or trade show display theme, you’ll be thrilled to hear about GenStone’s new custom coloring option!

Now, you can get custom-colored faux stone panels, corner pieces, trim, and ledgers manufactured using colors that match your brand. This is a fantastic way to truly make your GenStone faux stone trade show display an integrated part of your overall brand message.

Here’s how it works:

- Upon your approval of the virtual sample, we’ll take your order and get to work producing your custom-colored faux stone, which will be shipped within 2-4 weeks.

At GenStone, we’re passionate about bringing the look of real stone to customers all over the country, but without the real stone price!

Custom Colored Faux Brick Paneling

When it comes to customizing a trade show display that is as unique as it is on-brand, a faux stone treatment from GenStone can’t be beat.

And don’t forget: after you’ve completed your faux stone trade show display project, be sure to snap a photo and send it to us. We love showcasing customer installations on our ‘Projects’ page. 

Good luck from your friends at GenStone!

text:
5 Fireplace & TV Wall Ideas That Actually Work

Alex Padilla
Project Coordinator

Designing a fireplace wall with a TV can feel like a compromise. Too often, one ends up too high, too dominant, or out of proportion with the rest of the space. The right layout brings both elements together into a single, cohesive focal point that looks intentional and functions comfortably. Here are 5 fireplace and TV wall ideas that actually work in real homes.
Try Visualizer Get Project Planning Guide

The most absolutely simple product to work with. Looks Great, totally transformed our fireplace with ease.

  William’s Gray Stone Fireplace

Keystone

Idea #1: Stacked Stone Fireplace with Centered TV

A stacked stone fireplace creates a strong focal point that naturally anchors the entire room. Mounting the TV directly above keeps the layout symmetrical and visually balanced without competing elements.

This setup works especially well in living rooms where the fireplace is already the main feature, allowing both the TV and fireplace to feel integrated rather than separate.

Faux Stone Fireplace

Idea #2: Stone Fireplace with TV Built Into the Wall

Integrating the TV into the fireplace wall creates a seamless, built-in look that feels custom without requiring major construction. The stone texture adds depth while the TV placement keeps everything clean and intentional.

This approach is ideal for modern spaces where homeowners want a streamlined design without sacrificing warmth or character.

Rick’s DIY Stone Fireplace

Design Tips

- Keep the center of your TV close to seated eye level whenever possible

- Make sure your fireplace allows proper heat clearance for electronics

- Use the same material across the wall to unify the design

- Plan for hidden wiring to keep the final result clean

Idea #3: Fireplace Surround Over Existing Brick

Updating an old brick fireplace with a stone surround instantly modernizes the space while maintaining the original structure. Adding a TV above allows the entire wall to function as a refreshed focal point.

This works particularly well in renovation projects where you want a major visual upgrade without a full rebuild.

Faux Stone Fireplace with an Antique Mantel

Idea #4: Wood Stove Surround with Stone Wall

A stone surround around a wood stove creates a cozy, grounded focal point that pairs naturally with a mounted TV above or nearby. The added texture helps define the space without overwhelming it.

This setup is a great option for smaller rooms or cabins where space is limited but style still matters.

Heath’s Faux Stone Wood Stove Surround

Idea #5: Fireplace Wall Designed for TV Placement

Designing the fireplace wall specifically with TV placement in mind ensures proper proportions, spacing, and functionality from the start. This creates a cleaner, more intentional layout compared to retrofitting a TV later.

This approach works best in new builds or planned renovations where layout decisions can be made upfront.

Dana’s Faux Stone Gas Fireplace

FAQs
Ask Away. We've Heard it All.

Can you mount a TV above a fireplace?

Yes, but it depends on heat output and clearance. Electric fireplaces offer the most flexibility, while traditional units may require additional spacing or a mantel.

Do fireplace and TV walls need to match?

They don’t have to match exactly, but using consistent materials or colors helps create a cohesive look.

What is the best height for a TV above a fireplace?

Ideally, the center of the TV should be close to eye level when seated. If the fireplace forces it higher, consider a tilting mount to improve viewing comfort.

Jason Slee

Project Coordinator

What type of fireplace works best with a TV?

Electric fireplaces are the most flexible, but properly designed gas or wood-burning fireplaces can also work with the right clearances.

See how adding stone transformed this home’s exterior creating contrast, structure, and a more finished look without major construction.

Part of the home’s exterior had become worn, mismatched, and visually unappealing. It stood out from the rest of the house—and not in a good way.

The homeowner didn’t want to rip everything out or deal with a full siding replacement. They just wanted a clean way to cover the problem and make it look intentional again.

Instead of removing the existing surface, we installed stone directly over it—creating a clean, finished look that blends with the rest of the home.

✅ Installed directly over existing surface

✅ No demolition required

✅ Completed in hours, not days

After

Can GenStone be installed indoors and outdoors?

Yes. GenStone panels are designed for both interior and exterior applications. They are commonly used for accent walls, fireplace surrounds, entryways, garages, outdoor kitchens, and exterior facades.

Evan Trevenna

Senior Project Coordinator

Are GenStone panels weather resistant?

Yes. GenStone panels are designed to withstand outdoor conditions including rain, snow, and temperature changes, making them suitable for exterior projects.

Amanda Lombard

Director

How long does a typical GenStone project take?

Most GenStone projects can be completed in a single afternoon or weekend depending on the size of the space. Because the panels are lightweight and designed to interlock, homeowners can install them much faster than traditional masonry stone.

Courtney Mintz

Project Coordinator

Do I need special tools to install GenStone panels?

No special masonry tools are required. Most projects can be completed using common tools like a circular saw, screws, a drill, and a level. The panels are easy to cut and install using standard woodworking tools.

Kevin O'Dwyer

Can You Install Stone Over a Chimney?

Yes, GenStone can be installed over any flat surface as long as the substrate is structural. To install over concrete, brick or stucco we recommend using Tapcon screws and construction adhesive. For all other substrates, deck screws are the recommended fastener.

Is It Safe for Exterior Chimneys?

Yes, GenStone is engineered for exterior use and will endure the elements like any other siding product.

Does This Work on Wood or Siding?

GenStone can be installed over any flat, sturdy surface.

How Long Does Installation Take?

GenStone is as simple as measure, cut and attach. A chimney like the one featured in this article would take two people about a day and a half and one person no longer than two or three days to complete.

Popular Texas home improvement ideas include upgrading patios, outdoor kitchens, porch columns, entryways, garage accents, fireplace surrounds, and exterior siding details. How can I improve curb appeal on a Texas home? Add contrast and texture to visible exterior areas like the entryway, garage, porch, columns, and lower siding. Faux stone panels can help create a custom look without a full exterior remodel. Is faux stone a good option for Texas homes? Yes. Faux stone works well for Texas homes because it adds the look of stone while staying lightweight, low maintenance, and easier to install than traditional masonry. GenStone Pillar Panels are designed to cover an 8 inch square post while the columns are 17 inches square. The pillars can be terminated into the ceiling or capped with a 13.50 inch square flat or peaked cap. The caps are also available for columns in both a flat and peaked option, the column caps are 23 inches square.

Use the filter below to sort our stone pillar and stone column products.

Pillar Panels 101

The each stone pillar panel is 48 inches tall can be either stacked vertically for taller posts or cut down for shorter posts. If your post is smaller than 8 inches square, you can simply fur your post out with one or two vertical furring strips on each side of the post. If your post is larger than 8 inches, we suggest our column kits for posts up to 17 inches square or our stacked stone panels for posts that are larger than 17 inches square.

Note: you will need 4 pillar panels to cover a 48 inch tall post as shown in the pictures.

Columns 101

GenStone column kits are are completed by attaching four GenStone 90º outside corner panels. The corner panels are 23.50 inches tall and can be stacked vertically to create any size stone column. The column examples below were created with eight outside corners and one flat column cap.

text:
Project Pricing FAQs

Outside vs Inside Corners

GenStone 90º outside and inside corner panels are unique to the GenStone Made Easy system and are available in all stacked stone and brick colors. These carefully engineered panels eliminate the need to miter and deliver a visually uninterrupted transition between walls.

Ledgers

Each straight ledger delivers 3.50 linear feet of coverage and can be supplemented with outside and inside corner ledgers. The ledgers are used to finish the top of a wainscot installation and offer a sloped design ideal for shedding water.

Trim or No Trim

GenStone trim is available in all stacked stone and brick colors. Panels can terminate into the trim where it is used around obstacles such as hose bibs and electrical boxes. Trim can also be used to create a visual stopping point for partial wall installs.

Left and Right Finished Edges

Also called left and right returns, these 12″ x 12″ panels are available in all stacked stone colors. These panels can be used to wrap the stone around a corner or on a partially installed flat wall, providing an alternative to trim or painting the end of a panel.

The GenStone 90º Outside Corner panel can also be used to create a stone column. As opposed to GenStone Pillar Panels which are designed to encase an 8-inch square post, 4 Outside Corners fit seamlessly around a 17-inch square post.

If your post is less than 17 inches on each side, you can fur the post out with wood strips on each side b... Expand full text

The GenStone 90º Outside Corner panel can also be used to create a stone column. As opposed to GenStone Pillar Panels which are designed to encase an 8-inch square post, 4 Outside Corners fit seamlessly around a 17-inch square post.

If your post is less than 17 inches on each side, you can fur the post out with wood strips on each side before attaching the panels. Each Outside Corner also provides 22.50 inches of height coverage making measuring how many panels you will need easy.

To determine how many panels you need, measure the height of your column in inches and then divide that measurement by 22.50 in order to find out how many rows of 4 corner panels you will need.

GenStone Pillar Panels are designed to wrap an 7.75 inch square post. Each panel is 24 inches tall and can be stacked vertically for taller posts or cut down for shorter posts. The panels can be terminated into a ceiling or finished with one of our flat or peaked pillar caps.

Four GenStone 90º corner panels are designed to fit together around a 16.75 inch post. The corner panels are 22.50 inches tall can be stacked vertically or cut down for accommodate a certain height. GenStone faux stone wall panels are on sale now ! GenStone is cast from real stone and hand painted with 12 coats of premium paint to deliver the authentic shapes, texture and shadows found throughout a natural stone wall. GenStone faux stone wall panels are accompanied by our one of a kind 14 piece Made Easy System of corners, ledgers, trim and more.

This easy to install panelized system goes from the box to the wall in minutes making any interior or exterior faux stone project achievable for the ordinary homeowner without mortar and mess. Starting with the faux stone wall panels below, use the filter to view the entire GenStone system or click into the color of your choice to see projects and the pieces used from the system of the particular color that you are considering.

Need Help? Tap Project SOS and we will assign your project to a Project Coordinator out of our office in Colorado . Your Project Coordinator will guide you through color selection, how much GenStone you need and be your single point of contact for any installation questions you may have along the way.

With GenStone, you can have the look of stone or brick without the mortar and mess. More importantly, we’ve engineered the labor out of the install, so GenStone is DIY friendly and costs about 50% less than masonry work. GenStone fastens to any existing flat surface including wood, brick, stucco, concrete and drywall. There’s no need to remove any existing material.

The GenStone stacked stone and brick installation systems are designed to make any project from remodels to renovations, pillars, columns and even upgrading the curb appeal of a steel building simple for everyone. Watch the videos below for a quick overview on how each component of our made easy system works together to help you complete your project quickly and easily.

Now that you’re convinced you can improve your property with GenStone, it’s time to plan your project. You will need the length and height of each wall you plan to install GenStone on in order to determine how many panels, corners, trim and ledgers you will need. We’ve included some helpful resources below to assist you in this process, after you record your measurements, head to our project calculator to input your dimensions and we will tell you how much GenStone you will need for your project.

title: Return Policy - GenStone
description: Before ordering the GenStone product for your project, please refer to our return policy for full, partial and damaged product returns.
text:
RETURN POLICY

Thank you for your purchase. We hope you are happy with your purchase. However, if you are not completely satisfied with your purchase for any reason, you may return it to us for a full refund subject to the Special Considerations outlined below. Please see below for more information on our return policy.

RETURNING PRODUCT

All returns must be postmarked within ninety (90) days of the delivery date. All returned items must be in new and unused condition, with all original tags and labels attached.

RETURN PROCESS

To return an item, send an email to [email protected] with your name, order number and a list of the items you are returning.

Please note, you will be responsible for all return shipping charges. We strongly recommend that you use a trackable method to mail your return.

REFUNDS

After receiving your return and inspecting the condition of your item, we will process your return. Please allow at least ten (10) days from the receipt of your item to process your return. Refunds may take 1-2 billing cycles to appear on your credit card statement, depending on your credit card company. We will notify you by email when your return has been processed.

COLOR EXCHANGE AFTER FULFILLMENT

If your order has been delivered and is still in new condition or is in transit, you may exchange colors, however each exchange will be subject to the cost to ship the current order back to the closest GenStone warehouse and the cost to ship the new color to you. If you placed your order with a Project Coordinator (PC) at GenStone, contact your PC to process the exchange. If you purchased your order on genstone.com, contact our customer service department at 1-800 -425 -0788 to begin an exchange.

CANCELLATIONS

If you choose to cancel your order and GenStone has already incurred costs associated with fulfilling your order, your refund may be subject to cancellation fees.

EXCEPTIONS

The following items cannot be returned:

- Damaged products including panels and accessories that have been installed.

For defective or damaged products, please contact us at the customer service number below to arrange a refund or exchange.

SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS

- Full Returns: A 25% restocking fee will be charged for returns containing the full original order or mostly full orders to be determined at GenStone’s sole discretion.

- Partial Returns: Customers who return only a portion of the original order because the customer ordered too much product for their project are not subject to the restocking fee.

- Refunds will be processed after the warehouse verifies the number of products that are in good condition and can be checked back into inventory.

- Customers who return a portion of the original order can contact GenStone to receive a return label after paying GenStone’s true cost for the label.

SHORTAGES AND DAMAGE

Once your GenStone is delivered, open each box and take inventory of the pieces you have received.
